question.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=4{x}^{2}+kx-2$ is $x=-1.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $-1.$ 

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c$ is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}.
$$

Substituting $a=4$ and $b=k$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{k}{2(4)} \\  & =-\frac{k}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-1,$ so we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{k}{8} & =-1 \\ -k & =-8 \\ k & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
